meta.title: Renewable Energy Development Zones (REDZ), South Africa
gazettes: GN 114, Government Gazette 41445, 16 Feb 2018 - REDZ 1-8 (Minister Molewa)
GN 142/144/145, Government Gazette 44191, 26 Feb 2021 - REDZ 9-11 (Minister Creecy)
meta.effect: A large-scale wind or solar PV facility inside a REDZ needs only a Basic Assessment rather than a full Environmental Impact Assessment - roughly 147 days against 300.
meta.TECHNOLOGY MATTERS: Five REDZs are gazetted for SOLAR PV ONLY. A wind project there gets no streamlining. Check the technology field, not just the location.
meta.BOUNDARIES ARE APPROXIMATE: The gazetted REDZs are irregular polygons. This file holds a CENTRE POINT and an equivalent-area RADIUS (sqrt(area/pi)) as a circular approximation, because we do not hold the official shapefiles. Use it to decide whether a site is worth checking - never as a determination. The authoritative screening tool is the DFFE Environmental GIS portal.
meta.areas_source: CSIR Strategic Environmental Assessment Phase 1 (2015) published zone areas; Phase 2 (2019) for REDZ 9-11.
meta.purpose: REDZs concentrate utility-scale wind and solar into areas the state has already assessed as suitable, through two Strategic Environmental Assessments (CSIR, 2015 and 2019). They serve two ends: FAST-TRACKED APPROVAL - a Basic Assessment instead of a full EIA - and SMOOTHER GRID INTEGRATION, since the zones were gazetted alongside five Strategic Transmission Corridors so that generation clusters where network investment is planned. GN 145 of 2021 sets a separate streamlined procedure for electricity grid infrastructure inside a REDZ.
meta.polygons_not_held: The official REDZ boundaries are published as shapefiles and KMZ on the DFFE E-GIS portal, but downloading them requires registration and the portal proved unreachable across repeated attempts on 17 Aug 2026 (connection dropped every time; data.gov.za and an ArcGIS Hub mirror also failed). No public mirror was found. This file therefore holds centre points and equivalent-area radii, and every output on the site states that boundaries are approximate. NOT PLANNED WORK: chasing the portal further was judged not worth the effort, because the approximation already catches the error that actually costs money - the five SOLAR-ONLY zones, where a wind developer assuming 'Upington is a REDZ' would budget months too little. IF THE FILES EVER TURN UP - most likely from an environmental assessment practitioner, a developer, SAWEA/SAPVIA or CSIR, all of whom use them as working files - converting to GeoJSON and swapping the radius screening for a point-in-polygon test is a short job, and the 'approximate boundaries' caveat could then come off.
meta.licence_note: Licence covers this compilation - the assembly, correction and structuring of the underlying data. Source data remains under its own terms; see the source field.

zones.name: Emalahleni
zones.note: Declared partly for the just transition - Emalahleni is the heart of the coal complex. Gazetted for solar PV only, which drew criticism given the local wind resource.
